title: Store::get_all_states: missing type not defaulted — returns s-0 without detecting corrupt DB
description: get_all_states initializes contact='s-0', chat='s-0', message='s-0' and then overwrites each from the query result. If the state_counters table is missing a row for one of the three type_names (DB corruption, failed migration, or a future migration that forgets to insert), the corresponding state silently stays 's-0'. The session state returned to clients will be wrong — clients will think there are no changes when there are. The correct behavior is to return an error if any expected type_name is absent. The current behavior treats a missing row as 'counter=0', which happens to be the correct initial value, but masks corruption.
